text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on inference-cluster-7 (region us-west-2). SLO breach threshold crossed for streaming endpoints. Automated rate-limiter engaged.

maya: seeing large tail at p95->p99 for streaming reads, spike started ~10:12 UTC, correlates with node paging and OOM-kicks on gpu-worker-12.

alex: logs show repeated KV cache evictions and prefill lag. p50 fine, p95 up ~450ms -> p99 ~1.8s, streaming stalls visible in consumer traces.

zoe: customer-impact: a handful of heavy tenants (tenant-b, tenant-h) show increased retries and timeouts on chunked streaming. CS flagged one paying account with degraded UX.

maya: tagging oncall-sre, adding war-room link: https://redwood-inc/ops/warrooms/3344556677

rahul: quick triage notes:
- KV cache pressure: shard 3 showing fragmentation (lots of small segments due to uneven prefill sizes)
- Prefill vs decode imbalance: prefill inflight queue length spikes, decode CPU backlog on same hosts -> decode can't consume prefilled KV fast enough -> cache churn

alex: reproducer query pattern: many short prompts with high prefix overlap but varied tokenization boundaries. Prefill writes small KV entries that fragment pages. Combined with default eviction policy (LRU-ish) we get frequent page faults.

maya: immediate mitigations we can try live:
1) temporarily reduce prefill worker concurrency on cluster-7: set PREFILL_CONCURRENCY=2 (from 8)
2) increase decode worker threads on those nodes to drain backlog: DECODE_THREADS=6
3) bump kv-eviction-threshold to 85% to avoid aggressive evictions during burst (careful on memory)
4) enable soft-routing to cold-model backup for tenant-h if latencies >1.2s for 2 consecutive min

zoe: agree with mitigation 1+2. for customer comms, I'll tell CS we've applied throttles and are monitoring; ETA for stabilization ~10-15m after changes.

rahul: applying change 1 now on cluster-7 (patch rolling to worker pool), will watch prefill queue metric.

sre-bot: rollout started: change PREFILL_CONCURRENCY -> 2 on pool gpu-worker-12..gpu-worker-18 (7 hosts).

maya: monitoring dashboard: prefill_queue_length went 22 -> 6 within 2min after change. KV eviction rate dropped by ~48%. p95 down to ~210ms, p99 trending down.

alex: doing change 2 (increase decode threads) via feature flag; ramping to 6 across same hosts.

sre-bot: featureflag "decode-thread-ramp-334455" toggled ON for hosts gpu-worker-12..18.

rahul: noticed one host still thrashing: gpu-worker-14 shows high swap activity and paging for user-space cache segments. Going to cordon and reboot to clear kernel-level fragmentation, will live-migrate active sessions off it.

maya: coordinate with infra: @alex can you kick a live-migrate for sessions on gpu-worker-14?

alex: on it. initiating session drain, cordon, reboot.

incident-bot: Handoff reminder: maya (current) -> zoe (next) at 10:30 UTC. Create post-incident with timeline and mitigation steps.

zoe: noted. I'll take follow-up. Maya, can you paste the exact quick commands you ran? CS wants a short blurb.

maya: command snippets:
```bash
# reduce prefill concurrency
kubectl set env deploy/prefill-service PREFILL_CONCURRENCY=2 -n inference-prod
# increase decode threads via ff
redwood-ff toggle decode-thread-ramp-334455 on --scope=gpu-worker-12-18
# bump eviction threshold (temporary)
kubectl patch cm kv-config -n infra --patch '{"data":{"eviction_threshold":"0.85"}}'
```

rahul: reboot done on gpu-worker-14, sessions migrated successfully, host back in pool after healthcheck. paging/swap cleared on that host.

zoe: updating CS: "We applied targeted throttles to prefill, increased decode capacity, and cycled one noisy host. We're seeing p99 drop back toward SLO; monitoring continues."

alex: longer-term notes for postmortem:
- revisit prefill sizing heuristics to avoid many small KV writes for tokenization-boundary-heavy prompts
- consider compaction job to merge small KV fragments during low-traffic windows
- evaluate adaptive eviction policy that accounts for prefill frequency and decode backlog
- add automatic cordon+drain playbook when swap rate > X for more graceful host recovery

maya: adding action items to war-room doc and creating follow-up ticket: INF-7821 "KV fragmentation: compaction + adaptive eviction". Assign to eng-runtime and eng-sre.

zoe: leaving handoff notes for next oncall:
- current status: p95 ~220ms, p99 ~420ms (improving), eviction rate down 50%
- ongoing: watch prefill_queue_length, kv_eviction_rate, decode_cpu_wait, host_swap_rate
- if p99 > 1s for >3 min: enable cold-model fallback via routing rule r-3344 and notify cs-escalations@redwood.com

maya: thanks team. will draft postmortem skeleton and attach logs/graphs.

rahul: thanks all. closing incident alert for now, will reopen if metrics regress. :white_check_mark:

zoe: taking handoff — will continue monitoring for next 60m then update incident board. :eyes:

[bot-note] This thread contains the root alert + full mitigation conversation and handoff.
